sections.solution: OSA I ECO PUZZLE is a comprehensive support programme for families that include adults on the autism spectrum (OSA). The programme is made up of several components (puzzle pieces) that form a compact and coherent whole. As a result of taking part in the programme, families with OSA form a self-help group that supports the activities of OSA, gives whole families space for social and income-generating activity, and looks after both the natural and the emotional environment.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the insufficient number of offers for families with an adult on the autism spectrum (OSA) that support work and social activity and strengthen relationships within and outside the family.
sections.whoCanUse: Adults on the autism spectrum, their families and those close to them.
sections.doesItWork: The innovation effectively met parents’ needs related to social contact, sharing experiences, contact with a psychologist, and seeing their children in a different environment and in a different light. Their satisfaction with taking part was very high. The tests carried out positively verified the mechanism leading to the intended effects. The assumptions leading to changes in the target group were met, and the effects were particularly visible in increased knowledge, the acquisition of skills in making eco-friendly hygiene products, and opportunities to earn an income. Clearly positive effects were also achieved in psychological coping with challenges; however, due to the complexity of the families’ situations and the many dimensions of their problems, this effect could only be initiated in the target group.

c068.title: Blind and partially sighted people as Polish language teachers

sections.solution: A model for supporting Polish language teaching for migrants, delivered by blind people. It consists of a Polish language course designed to meet the needs of blind and partially sighted people who act as teachers. In addition, the model includes support materials, such as lesson plans with presentations, audio dramas, songs, texts, etc., and materials for tutors on improving their Polish language teaching skills.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the difficulty blind and partially sighted people face in finding work suited to their needs and abilities, and the difficulty migrants/refugees face in adapting and taking up work.
sections.targetGroup: Migrants from eastern countries who, on arriving in Poland, cannot speak Polish well enough to communicate; people with visual impairments.
sections.whoCanUse: Language schools, organisations helping people with visual impairments into work, employers of migrants.
sections.doesItWork: Implementing the innovation resulted in an effective model for supporting Polish language teaching for migrants, delivered by blind people. Thanks to the course, adapted to the needs of blind and partially sighted people, the teachers gained tools that allow them to teach effectively. Support materials, such as lesson plans with a variety of audio and text elements, helped to improve the quality and variety of the lessons. Furthermore, the materials for tutors helped to improve Polish language teaching skills, which ensures that blind people deliver the course professionally and effectively. Overall, the innovation contributed to more effective Polish language teaching for migrants and greater access to education for blind people in the role of teachers.

c070.title: Passport for patients with a rare disease

sections.solution: The passport is an IT solution that stores the most important information about the disease, medicines and the doctors treating a patient with a rare disease. This information is kept on an electronic device that the patient can always carry with them. The system consists of: a web application, into which medical staff at the Reference Centre enter the necessary data about the patient's disease; an electronic chip, on which the patient's card data and standards of care are stored; and an NFC chip programmer.
sections.problems: A rare disease often requires special treatment methods, or certain symptoms may be a reason not to use a particular treatment. For many rare diseases, treatment standards have already been developed and are shared by international organisations. Unfortunately, in the Polish system, treatment standards for rare diseases are not widely used by doctors who do not specialise in rare diseases.
sections.targetGroup: Patients with rare diseases
sections.whoCanUse: Doctors, physiotherapists – this group can use the passport, promote the solution in their community and develop further disease specifications (as part of the innovation, cards were created for 3 rare diseases: Duchenne muscular dystrophy, Williams syndrome and Marfan syndrome). Parents, patients with a rare disease – this group can use the passport, promote the solution in their community and raise interest in the topic among organisations representing patients with rare diseases.
sections.doesItWork: Parents of children with a rare disease, patients and doctors all rated the passport for patients with a rare disease positively. They particularly noted the accurate and expert description of the rare disease, which was prepared by doctors who work with rare diseases.

sections.solution: “Pełna wokanda” is a board game for people with intellectual disabilities. The tool contains materials, questions, content, tips and tasks focused on preparing for a court hearing, taking part in it, talking to a lawyer, giving evidence, and the steps needed after the case has ended. Parts of the game explain difficult terms, give tips on where to look for information, and involve players in the tasks that need to be done at each stage.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the lack of tools that allow people with intellectual disabilities to gain, in an effective way, the knowledge and skills needed to prepare for taking part in court proceedings.
sections.targetGroup: The innovation is aimed at adults with intellectual disabilities
sections.whoCanUse: Organisations working for people with intellectual disabilities, including Occupational Therapy Workshops (Warsztaty Terapii Zajęciowej), Community Self-Help Centres (Środowiskowe Domy Samopomocy) and NGOs.
sections.doesItWork: The game can be an effective tool to help increase knowledge and gain the skills needed when dealing with the justice system. Although a longer testing period is needed for all the positive effects to show, and it was not possible to observe all the effects planned in the project, there are signs that it is effective. In particular, effects were seen in reinforcing basic knowledge about the court (who the claimant is, male or female, and what the court is) and in understanding situations (including practical ones, such as why bags are checked at the entrance). Other important positive effects also appeared, such as increased self-confidence, memory training, practice in working in a group, and enjoyable competition in educational activities.

c074.title: Piosenki uczestniczące (Participatory Songs)

sections.solution: Original compositions and educational songs adapted to how children perceive the world – above all children who do not speak and children with communication difficulties. Thanks to this solution, these children can take an active part in musical play, from which they were excluded until now.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to limited access to tools for active social and educational inclusion aimed at children who cannot communicate verbally or whose communication is incomplete or unclear.
sections.targetGroup: Children aged 1-3 who do not speak or have communication difficulties and cannot communicate verbally, and children whose communication is incomplete or unclear.
sections.whoCanUse: Parents and carers, care facilities, specialist counselling centres, nursery schools and crèches.
sections.doesItWork: Tests showed that playing together in a group with the support of the tool and musical instruments helps improve concentration, strengthens the shared identity among group members, and helps develop expressive and receptive speech. The tool also proved useful in supporting parents working with their children at home. The children taking part in the project felt special because they had their own songbook and knew the songs being sung. The children (except the two youngest) were keen to point to things in the booklets and to show gestures. Some of the children learned to sing and to use simple phrases in the song.

The children's parents and teachers said that, thanks to the training, the children were able to get on a train, go into a station or enter a hotel for the first time.

c076.title: Portable modular bathrooms

sections.solution: A portable bathroom built from modules that can be carried in and installed in rooms not designed for standard sanitary facilities (e.g. attics, basements, hallways). A modular bathroom makes it possible to install basic fittings such as a shower, washbasin, toilet and ventilation, and to give access to a bathroom to families who previously had none.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the lack of access to a private bathroom in the home where people live. It allows people to meet their physiological needs and look after their hygiene without feeling ashamed, and it reduces social isolation.
sections.targetGroup: People on low incomes and people living in homes without a bathroom who cannot install one, e.g. because the ownership of the property has not been legally settled.
sections.whoCanUse: Municipal offices, social welfare centres, county family support centres (PCPR), NGOs supporting people on low incomes.
sections.doesItWork: Modular bathrooms improve the comfort of life and mental well-being of the people who use them. They allow people to meet their physiological needs in the home where they already live. Importantly, running costs (e.g. electricity and water use) stay at the same level, which matters to the people who use the innovation. c077.title: Guide for people with ASD "Moje potrzeby - gdzie i jak je realizować?" (My needs – where and how to meet them?)

sections.solution: The innovation is a guide using words and pictures for young people and adults with autism spectrum disorders (hereinafter ASD) about places and ways to meet everyday and basic needs outside the home. Its main parts are: an activity plan (showing what needs to be done, step by step), behavioural scripts (suggesting what to say and when) and AAC – augmentative and alternative communication methods (graphic symbols).
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the low level of social skills and the specific difficulties people with ASD have in learning behaviours, which require special behavioural learning procedures (i.e. they do not know how to behave, find it hard to tell appropriate from inappropriate behaviour, do not know what to say and when, etc.).
sections.targetGroup: People diagnosed with ASD (autism or Asperger syndrome) in adolescence (up to the age of 13) or adulthood who can read and have basic communication skills.
sections.whoCanUse: Special schools, public schools with special classes, non-public schools, support facilities for people with ASD.
sections.doesItWork: The guide clearly had a positive effect on the independence of people with ASD. Small steps and learning basic activities and behaviours turned out to be a big change for people with ASD and those around them. Besides a greater sense of independence, the people testing the product also showed – linked to independence – a stronger sense of agency and of being able to make decisions.

sections.problems: The innovation responds to the shortage of educational aids for blind children. There is a lack of products that are attractive to children and at the same time support different areas of their development.
sections.targetGroup: Blind or partially sighted children.
sections.whoCanUse: Teachers at schools for blind children, as well as parents of children with visual impairments, and NGOs supporting this group of children.
sections.doesItWork: Both the children and the teachers at the school for blind people rated the 3D puzzles positively. They particularly noted the three-dimensional form, the interesting shapes and the child-friendly theme, which is animals. The project responds to the needs of teachers and parents, who, thanks to the puzzles, have access to dedicated toys that support the learning and education, as well as the play, of blind children.

sections.solution: "Rodzinny system wzajemnej pomocy" is a model for the social inclusion of adults with autism aged 20–26 who have finished their education, are not continuing it and are also not in work. The innovation is based on a model of occupational and inclusive therapy that would work best in a home, "family" setting. It would help the target group develop social skills and practical, work-related skills, support social integration in the local community, the family and the neighbourhood, and provide respite for the families and carers of people with ASD.
sections.problems: The innovation addresses social problems faced by adults with autism who are not in education or work, such as: No activities on offer for autistic people over the age of 24, especially activities that prepare them for work on the open labour market Occupational Therapy Workshops (Warsztaty Terapii Zajęciowej) that do not meet the needs of people with autism (groups that are too large, no option to calm down, etc.) No places, or a limited number of places, at Occupational Therapy Workshops (Warsztaty Terapii Zajęciowej) After the age of 24, autistic people cannot continue their education, and the only options available are Community Self-Help Centres (Środowiskowe Domy Samopomocy) or Occupational Therapy Workshops (Warsztaty Terapii Zajęciowej), where autistic people may find a place in large groups with changing staff. However, there are often not enough places for everyone who wants to take part in the workshops, and in addition the workshops are not adapted to their needs No opportunities to develop skills, including skills needed to find work Limited effectiveness of therapy and of improving the social functioning of people with autism The solutions used so far are often seen as superficial and do not prepare people with severe autism for life in society or for managing everyday tasks The mental strain and time burden on carers of autistic people over the age of 24 who provide care on their own Carers of autistic people are under exceptional strain because they have to care for their adult child. Alternating care would give carers temporary respite.
sections.targetGroup: Adults with autism aged 20–26 who have finished their education, are not continuing it, are not in work and have not been accepted into an Occupational Therapy Workshop (WTZ), and their informal carers who look after them every day.
sections.whoCanUse: This is an offer that can be put into practice in a home, family or neighbourhood setting and given a regular, professional and optimal format, but it may be difficult to scale up. Scaling up requires reaching informal groups, informal carers and parents of adults with ASD, which in practice may be an additional challenge in the strategy for spreading the innovation. Informal groups of this kind, which work individually and flexibly, should also be prepared to implement the model, trained and supported with specialist advice.
sections.doesItWork: The proposed solution is aimed at people with ASD who have a certificate of mild disability, as they should respond best to therapy and rehabilitation. Regular meetings in small groups in the family homes of these people were intended to help participants build relationships and feel safe, so that specific activities based on each person's preferences and interests could then be carried out in a familiar setting, within a familiar group. The project is very useful for the people taking part in it. However, because it was carried out quickly, not all activities could be run on an alternating care basis, which would have added value for parents and could have given them real respite.

c082.title: Ścieżka motosensoryczna (motor-sensory path)

sections.solution: The motor-sensory path is designed to help people who, because of reduced physical fitness, feel anxious and have stopped using the town's public spaces to get used to urban space again. The architectural and urban design of the stations for training fine motor skills, located in public space, includes: a design for a path made up of stations that use the natural features of the space, so that exercises can be done "along the way" during a walk, a shopping trip or a visit to the doctor; the option to arrange the space and configure the stations depending on the site conditions, the available budget, the planned level of difficulty or the user group; instruction boards with pictograms, which allow people to do the exercises on their own; a mobile app with instructional videos and sets of exercises linked to specific stations;
sections.problems: The "Ścieżka moto-sensoryczna" makes it possible to do rehabilitation "along the way", while carrying out everyday activities, such as going to the shop, the health clinic, etc. Its advantage is financial flexibility in implementation: existing elements of the space's infrastructure can be used and adapted as exercise stations, and the project can be expanded or reduced as needed, which makes the costs of implementation very flexible.
sections.targetGroup: The solution is intended for older people and people with disabilities (with particular attention to impairments of the musculoskeletal system). Using the "Ścieżka moto-sensoryczna" will allow users to continue a therapy programme outside specialist physiotherapy centres, and as a result it may stop or slow down the decline in users' physical fitness.
sections.whoCanUse: The solution can be used by institutions, organisations, companies and individuals that have land that is open to the public or suitable for public use (municipalities (gmina), counties (powiat), medical or care facilities that have green areas, etc.).
sections.doesItWork: A location close to home helps users get used to outdoor conditions in their immediate surroundings, so that they can carry these positive experiences over to areas further away, allowing them to make full use of the town's cultural, educational and leisure offer.

sections.solution: “Ścieżka treningu umysłu” is a space for mental rehabilitation made up of 12 stations. It is designed to stimulate cognitive functions such as memory, logic and problem-solving, concentration, reflexes and attention, and analytical skills and thought processes. 4 stations of the trail are devoted to each of these functions, and all exercises have been designed at three levels of difficulty.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the problem of limited access to forms of rehabilitation and to the prevention of the decline of cognitive functions in older people.
sections.targetGroup: Older people with limited perception (mainly those showing the first symptoms of dementia) and people with intellectual disabilities.
sections.whoCanUse: Organisations that have spaces accessible to a wide range of users (the trails can be placed in city parks, on riverside boulevards or along walking routes), residential care homes, and institutions supporting people with intellectual disabilities.
sections.doesItWork: Using the trail helps to stimulate many cognitive functions and supports the process of mental rehabilitation. It improves memory, logic and problem-solving, concentration, reflexes and attention, and analytical skills and thought processes, which has a positive effect on quality of life. The solution was rated very highly by therapists and by the older people and people with intellectual disabilities who tested the tool. After the test, it was pointed out that the boards need to be adapted for outdoor use, i.e. boards that are not prototypes must be fully waterproof and frost-resistant so that all parts work properly and easily (they are intended for people with fine motor impairments and reduced physical fitness).

c084.title: Senior CUDER

sections.solution: "Senior CUDER" is a card game that aims to improve the functioning and quality of life of older people by strengthening their motivation and their ability to look after their health, and by improving their relationships with the people around them, including family and neighbours, and making new friends.
sections.problems: When working with older people, the game makes it possible to explore 5 problem areas: body: declining physical fitness and health problems; mind: problems with memory and concentration, declining intellectual abilities; spirituality: the risk of an extreme approach to spirituality (depressive tendencies or religious zealotry); emotions: low resilience, poor ability to cope with painful emotions related, for example, to loneliness or the passing of people of the same age; relationships: bonds with other people, for example an unmet need for closeness, emotional wounds and traumas that make it hard to build relationships.
sections.targetGroup: The game is intended for elderly people. It was designed both for people who function very well and are independent, and for those who need care where they live or stay.
sections.whoCanUse: The solution can be used by institutions, NGOs and organisations that provide care for older people, formal and informal groups that work with older people, and individuals who have an older person in their lives. It can also be a helpful tool for strengthening bonds with the people who look after an older person every day. The game is ideal for Seniors' Clubs, Senior Activity Centres, Care Homes, Senior Homes, long-term care facilities (ZOL), Day Care Centres, Sanatoriums and other places where meetings with older people take place.
sections.doesItWork: A session with "Senior CUDER" is an excellent opportunity to spend time together with other people, to get to know yourself and others, to deepen existing relationships and build new ones, and to improve the quality of every area of an older person's life. While keeping all the qualities of a social game and an attractive format, "Senior CUDER" can be a starting point for deeper reflection on one's own life, past experiences and the opportunities the player has now.

sections.solution: An online platform (a website also available in a mobile version for smartphones and tablets), aimed mainly at people with disabilities whose carers cannot go with them to cultural events (for example, to the cinema or theatre) because of other everyday duties. The platform makes it possible to connect people with disabilities who need a carer's support with users who can become so-called "temporary carers" when using cultural venues, for example when going to the cinema or theatre.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the limited access of people with disabilities to cultural venues, events and institutions.
sections.targetGroup: People with disabilities, especially those with a severe disability, and people who have difficulty moving around public spaces on their own.
sections.whoCanUse: Cultural, sports and leisure institutions, and organisers of cultural events.
sections.doesItWork: During the test it was not easy to recruit volunteers/temporary carers, and people with disabilities themselves were also not very interested in taking part. This was undoubtedly affected by the fact that the testing period fell during the most intense period of the pandemic, when many venues were closed to users. Test participants were worried about their health, and they also had limited trust in potential "temporary carers", in their commitment and in their real ability to provide assistance in a difficult situation.

c086.title: Stop otyłości - an innovative method of working with people with intellectual disabilities

sections.solution: The innovation is a method of working with people with intellectual disabilities who have class II and class III obesity. Its main aim is to make it easier to access professional and comprehensive support in the place where the person lives, including education and a tool for motivating the person with obesity and their closest circle, aimed at a lasting change in habits and lifestyle. The method also includes prevention of the obesity problem getting worse, so that community-based support can be provided for as long as possible and placement of the person in institutional care, such as a residential care home (DPS), can be avoided.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the high rate of class II and class III obesity among adults with intellectual disabilities.
sections.targetGroup: Adults with intellectual disabilities who have class II and class III obesity.
sections.whoCanUse: Facilities that support and activate people with intellectual disabilities in the local community, as well as staff of residential care facilities, strengthening their skills and working methods.
sections.doesItWork: The solution has proved effective in practice. During testing, the following were achieved among the members of the test group: improved laboratory test results (urine, blood count, creatinine, glucose, total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, triglycerides, ALT, AST, FT4, TSH), weight loss, improved health, and improved mood and well-being. At the same time, a possible difficulty was noted in maintaining the positive results of the test because of poor eating habits and an unhealthy lifestyle in the family environment of the person with an intellectual disability.

sections.solution: The main function of the app is to detect sound alarms, for example from carbon monoxide detectors and fire alarms, and to pass information about them to the user in a way the user has personalised. The methods of warning about danger available in the app are: vibrations, a torch, and emergency calls (a phone call to a chosen number if the user does not respond to notifications about a detected alarm). The app also records detected events in a history log.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the problems that Deaf/deaf and hard-of-hearing people face in hearing, receiving and recognising alerts and signals that indicate danger.
sections.targetGroup: Deaf/deaf people, hard-of-hearing people and deafblind people.
sections.whoCanUse: Private individuals, but above all hotels, guesthouses and student halls of residence, to improve the safety of guests with special needs.
sections.doesItWork: The app works effectively. It can detect an alarm signal and notify the user about it in a way that is accessible to them, and as a result wake them up and give them time to react and check the situation.

c088.title: Creating a tool to help older people settle inheritance matters correctly

sections.solution: An IT tool that, in a simple and intuitive way, makes it possible to identify the people entitled to inherit under statutory inheritance rules. The application also gives access to information about possible testamentary provisions and their forms. In addition, it allows users to set out their own circle of heirs, create a template will or find out whether a will needs to be drawn up by a notary.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the problem of limited access to information, tools and specialists that would allow older people with limited perception, who do not know how to draw up a legally valid will and dispose of their property according to their own wishes, to settle their inheritance situation.

sections.solution: Talerze zdrowia is a set of tools that will support older people and people with intellectual disabilities in learning how to prepare balanced meals. These simple teaching aids can be used both during workshops on healthy eating and by anyone who wants to prepare balanced meals on their own. The set includes 3 rotating discs placed one on top of another, called health plates (each disc shows different components of a balanced diet, which change depending on how the moving disc is set, so that a complete meal can be put together), and a book with simple, healthy dishes, instructions for preparing them and the basic rules for putting together healthy meals.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to older people's lack of skills in preparing properly balanced meals and to the lack of an easy-to-use tool that helps older people and people with disabilities (especially intellectual disabilities) gain practical knowledge about healthy eating.
sections.targetGroup: Older people, people with disabilities (especially intellectual disabilities), and people who want to learn the rules for preparing balanced meals.
sections.whoCanUse: People from the target group, municipal day care centres, residential care homes, senior activity centres, occupational therapy workshops, carers/family.
sections.doesItWork: The innovation is an easy-to-use and low-cost solution. After the testing period, users decided that it was necessary to add a sample shopping list to the recipe book and labels on the plates to make them easier to tell apart. Surveys carried out after the testing stage show that 100% of the testing group said that using „Talerze zdrowia” made it easier to prepare meals on their own (breakfast, lunch, dinner) and increased the amount of vegetables in their diet.

sections.doesItWork: Testing of the innovation showed it to be highly effective. The solution effectively supports dependent people, as well as their carers, in everyday life, strengthening their independence.

sections.solution: The innovation is an original method of high-mountain, wall and rock climbing involving people with visual impairments. The solution is intended as a form of rehabilitation and therapy through challenge: under the supervision of qualified instructors, conditions are created in which the guide and the blind person can develop ways of working together and communicating in a safe setting. The method involves preparing the climbing group in an indoor space (an artificial climbing wall) and then testing the skills they have gained in natural mountain conditions.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the limited access of people with visual impairments to mountain tourism.
sections.targetGroup: People with visual impairments
sections.whoCanUse: Sports facilities, organisations running mountain tourism for people with visual impairments, NGOs supporting people with visual impairments.
sections.doesItWork: To sum up the conclusions from the tests: climbing is a challenge, and many of its aspects cannot be mastered by organising training sessions with blind people without first improving their physical fitness. It would be advisable to organise additional sessions before the indoor wall training to support participants' fitness, such as gymnastics or endurance exercises. The training time preparing participants to take up climbing should therefore be planned somewhat differently. An additional distraction that made it harder to prepare the group for the climbing challenge was the difficult conditions at the indoor wall. There was noise all around, which did not always allow smooth communication between the climbers and the instructor, and this resulted in incomplete preparation for going outdoors. In such conditions, it would be advisable to use an electronic communication system. The outdoor challenge, on the other hand, proved very demanding for most participants, who, apart from poor physical fitness, did not feel confident among the rocks.

c101.title: Uważnione rodzieństwo

sections.solution: "Uważnione rodzieństwo" is a model for how parents of a child with a disability can act with their other, healthy children (the siblings of children with disabilities). The model is made up of a range of complementary tools that show the problems the siblings of a child with a disability may face, ways to avoid their negative effects and ways of coping with them. They are simple to use but also valuable – backed by psychological knowledge and useful for understanding and adapting to the situation.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the lack of comprehensive support for families (parents and siblings) into which a child with a disability is born, and to gaps in standardised procedures, support models and help for this group.
sections.targetGroup: Parents of children with disabilities, siblings of children with disabilities.
sections.whoCanUse: Support centres, psychological counselling centres, early development support centres.
sections.doesItWork: The innovation can be highly effective in achieving the planned positive results. In the opinion of the innovators and testers, it is an effective and valuable response to the lack of comprehensive information to support parents of children with disabilities, which is especially important in the early stage of coping with these challenges.

c102.title: Wibraap

sections.solution: Wibraap turns any sound into vibrations that can be felt on the body by a person wearing a “vest” connected to an app. The device (hardware) works together with an app (software) in a computer version and a mobile version. Users can choose for themselves how the device works: turning sound picked up by a microphone into vibrations (A), importing their own sound samples and then turning them into vibrations (B), or playing an electronic instrument.
sections.problems: d/Deaf and hard-of-hearing people are excluded from events where sound is the main medium. deaf/Deaf people do not have access to tools that would help them develop their creativity and sensitivity in perceiving sound and music in the broad sense, i.e. musical instruments (acoustic and electronic) and the experience of listening to music.
sections.targetGroup: d/Deaf and hard-of-hearing people.
sections.whoCanUse: The main users of this innovation could be: organisers of concerts and other music events, including shows and performances in which sounds play a big role. Potentially also philharmonic halls, musical theatres, cultural centres, and artists who would like to enrich and/or develop their shows based on experiencing music in ways other than hearing.
sections.doesItWork: Wibraap is a solution with huge potential, both for receiving music (“listening” to music) and for creative use – dance, composing, and jointly adding sound to artistic and educational “situations”. At the testing stage the device has reached, it needs further work and development, for example on the part that carries the device, i.e. the “vest” with the electronic equipment. The software part also has potential for development, by increasing its sound-processing capabilities and extending the software to other devices/operating systems. The tests also showed that deaf people valued the solution, and everyone who tested Wibraap wanted to keep the vests and use them every day.

c103.title: Rural support programme for people experiencing homelessness - Ścieżka Feniksa

sections.solution: The model of the rural support programme for people experiencing homelessness, “Ścieżka Feniksa”, combines the following elements: long-term, holistic support in the process of leaving homelessness within the local community an ecological approach and circular economy solutions in the therapeutic work process (for example: using recycled materials for work on the grounds of the reintegration centre, such as tyres, glass bottles, clay, recycled doors, plywood and plastic boxes, etc., creative reuse of materials, and using locally sourced natural materials such as branches, straw, wicker, etc.) use of local resources of the municipality (gmina) that are unused and overlooked solutions supporting the deinstitutionalisation of social services (moving away from institutional forms such as warming shelters, night shelters and hostels) and integration.
sections.problems: The project responds to the lack of long-term, holistic solutions for people experiencing homelessness in small municipalities, especially rural ones.
sections.targetGroup: People experiencing homelessness.
sections.whoCanUse: Municipalities (gminy), municipal social welfare centres (GOPS), and organisations supporting people experiencing homelessness.
sections.doesItWork: During testing, the mechanism leading to the effects was positively identified – the assumptions on which the changes depend were met. The effects that were particularly visible were related to increased motivation (above all, to stay in the recovery process – during testing, 9 out of 11 testers remained fully abstinent) and an increased sense of agency. It should also be noted that almost half of the 11 participants (5 people) said they would like to live and work in the countryside after the innovation ended. At the same time, it should be stressed that this is a high-risk innovation because it brings together the testing group (mobility, addictions, health problems) and the support provider, potentially a municipality, which, when making an investment, has to be guided by efficiency, regularity and certainty of achieving its goals.

c104.title: Multi-field dictionary of specialist terms PL-PJM

sections.solution: As part of the innovation, a mobile app was developed and tested. It is a multi-field PL-PJM (Polish – Polish Sign Language) dictionary, which works by adding videos of a specialist word being signed to the app. The app can grow as its users – Deaf people – add more specialist words. This allows the PL-PJM language communication system to develop. The app is a kind of Wikipedia in sign language.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the communication problems of Deaf people, which are linked, among other things, to the lack of a systematic, lasting way to record specialist terms in PJM (there is no official source or collection of signs).
sections.targetGroup: deaf/Deaf and hard of hearing people
sections.whoCanUse: Individual users (Deaf people who are specialists in particular fields), PL-PJM interpreters, universities and their staff.
sections.doesItWork: The idea of a multi-field dictionary is very well matched to the needs of the group. At present, however, the innovation is at a very early stage – it contains only a few entries, and it is hard to predict how quickly it will spread within the community. However, for the app to be truly useful, the solution must be promoted and continuously co-created by the Deaf community – without the community's involvement, the innovation will not grow or expand (and so its usefulness will be very limited).

sections.solution: A model for working with older people on passing on cultural and historical values related to applied art design and on developing older people's digital skills. As part of the innovation test, the following were created: a handbook describing the working method, a virtual gallery for older people, and 5 tutorials on: carrying out a needs assessment of older people, running photography workshops, setting up a virtual gallery, identifying and describing applied art objects, and storytelling.
sections.problems: The social innovation addresses problems related to the social exclusion of older people, caused by, among other things, weakened social relationships and isolation, weak intergenerational relationships and poor digital skills, which are among the key skills in today's society.
sections.targetGroup: Older people
sections.whoCanUse: Senior activity centres, local support groups for older people, NGOs, cultural institutions.
sections.doesItWork: The test showed a relatively low level of usefulness for the target group - although the testers gained some information about Polish design, they found it difficult to identify valuable objects in their surroundings. Without an accompanying expert, this would have been impossible, despite earlier visits to a museum (by part of the group). Although the innovation responds to older people's need to make and maintain contacts, the proposed format, while it helps improve skills in using a phone and taking photos, does not involve older people enough for them to use the resulting website themselves, post comments or publish their own stories in the gallery

sections.solution: A web portal with a set of practical information in Dari, which helps refugees from Afghanistan learn about and understand everyday life in Poland. The portal is divided into topic sections covering the most common areas of social life, such as health and education. It is not just translations of individual messages, but specific information placed in its cultural context. The portal also has information packs for the Polish side, for example for doctors or officials, which use simple descriptions and take the cultural context into account to give guidance on how to talk with Afghans.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the social exclusion of refugees from Afghanistan and to the communication and cultural barrier that prevents them from integrating successfully
sections.targetGroup: Refugees from Afghanistan
sections.whoCanUse: Organisations supporting refugees, help centres for foreigners, public offices, medical facilities
sections.doesItWork: The launch of the portal brought positive results, helping Afghan users understand life in Poland more easily and giving them a range of practical information about living in Poland. At the same time, Polish professionals gained knowledge about Afghan culture, which had a positive effect on meetings with the Afghan community and its integration in Poland.

sections.solution: A fencing wheelchair for athletes who use wheelchairs, meeting the following criteria: it can be operated independently by a person with disabilities, the product is lightweight, its price is lower than that of competition wheelchairs currently on the market, it uses modern composite materials and aluminium alloys.

c108.title: Support for mass events for people with visual impairments

sections.solution: Modular, mobile guidance mats that create safe walking routes for people with disabilities at concerts, festivals and inside buildings. The mats are equipped with ramps for people with mobility impairments, guide lines, underlays, contrast mats, warning areas and boundary lines along the edges. The solution is complemented by an instructional and information handbook intended for organisers of mass events. The handbook shows how to use these tools to organise a comfortable and accessible event.
sections.problems: The innovation addresses the problem of difficult or limited access to mass entertainment and cultural events for people with visual impairments.
sections.targetGroup: Blind and partially sighted people, as well as wheelchair users.
sections.whoCanUse: Organisers of mass events, concerts, outdoor events and performances, event companies, cultural institutions, festival offices, theatres, universities and conference organisers.
sections.doesItWork: Tests showed that the solution has huge potential and works very well as support in organising mass events, both indoors and outdoors. Different types of ground on which the mats are laid do not cause any difficulties in use, and the material the tool is made of proved to be versatile and suited to changing weather conditions (easy to clean, non-slip).

c109.title: Zakupy bez barier

sections.solution: A call-bell system that gives a dependent person discreet assistance while shopping. A trained shop employee supports the customer according to their needs, for example showing blind people where a product is located, and checking the ingredients, weight and use-by date. For wheelchair users, the employee will help them move between the aisles and reach products placed on high shelves.
sections.problems: Limited accessibility of self-service shops for people with disabilities, which makes it difficult for people with disabilities and older people to function independently.
sections.targetGroup: The solution is aimed at people with disabilities (for example blind people, people with mobility impairments, people with intellectual disabilities) and at older people.
sections.whoCanUse: Large-format shops and public bodies that can take on the coordination of „Zakupy bez barier” in their area (municipal offices, social welfare centres (OPS) or other bodies carrying out policy for older people and for people with disabilities).
sections.doesItWork: Testing showed that the solution is highly effective, making it easier, or even possible, for people with disabilities to do their shopping independently. Because the innovation is discreet, using it did not cause stigma or embarrassment.

c110.title: Shopping with one trolley with a child with a physical disability

sections.solution: A shopping trolley fitted with a contoured seat that allows a child with a disability (including a child with cerebral palsy) to be carried safely while shopping in large stores. The seat has a set of supports (including a headrest to support the head and the lower back) and a five-point safety harness. This solution helps to keep an upright and safe body position for a child whose body is floppy and whose muscle tone is significantly reduced.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the needs of carers of children with disabilities to do their shopping on their own, without having to arrange care for the child.
sections.targetGroup: Parents/carers of children with physical disabilities (including cerebral palsy).
sections.whoCanUse: Large stores, DIY stores, discount food shops.
sections.doesItWork: The solution was rated very highly by parents, assistants and children. During the test, suggestions were made to improve and better adapt the solution, such as making the headrest narrower and allowing its tilt to be adjusted, using harness straps that adjust automatically to the user, and making it possible to adjust the height of the footrests and shin guards.

sections.solution: As part of the social innovation, a multimedia mountain guide was prepared. sections.problems: The social innovation responds to the limited access that people with disabilities have to mountain tourism.
sections.targetGroup: People with physical and mobility disabilities, people with sensory disabilities, people with visual and hearing disabilities.
sections.whoCanUse: Local government in areas where mountain trails are located, PTTK, landscape parks and national parks, organisations working for tourism, organisations working for people with disabilities.
sections.doesItWork: During testing, people with various types of disabilities were able to explore mountain trails suited to their needs. In this way, barriers to accessing mountain tourism for people with disabilities were reduced. Thanks to audio description of the routes, with interesting facts about nature and recordings of the sounds of animals that can be found on the trail, people using the guide were able to broaden their knowledge and gain a lot of new, useful information. The testers responded very well to the multimedia guide. During meetings and consultations on the solution, participants pointed out the great attention to the needs of people with disabilities that the innovators had and showed. They noted the excellent audio description of the routes and the range of complementary information in the route descriptions.

c113.title: Sailing in the imagination – a way to overcome fears on the water

sections.solution: The innovation is a model for supporting older people (60+) and helping them overcome barriers and fear of boarding a yacht and sailing, and for enabling children and young people with physical disabilities to gain sailing experience using virtual reality. The innovation uses virtual reality goggles: users move their hands to control two virtual reality controllers, and all their movements and actions are reflected in the image they see. Training materials were also created for sailing instructors to go with the app, so that they can first learn how the VR app works themselves and then use this tool to teach other people.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the lack of access to sailing for people with physical disabilities and to fear of water.
sections.targetGroup: Older people with limited mobility and perception, young people and children with physical disabilities, people who are afraid of water.
sections.whoCanUse: Sailing and water tourism organisers, care centres for older people, institutions supporting people with physical disabilities.
sections.doesItWork: The app was rated positively by the test users and by sailing specialists. It was also presented at an international forum, where sailors from other countries greatly appreciated the idea. The test showed that by adding this kind of VR-based solution to sailing training, older people and children not only gain an additional element in their sailing education, but also have the opportunity to try modern VR technologies, which improves their digital skills.

c114.title: Zmysły w ruchu. A choreography model for blind people.

sections.solution: A model of movement and choreography work in the form of an electronic publication and audio files containing movement and choreography exercises for people with visual impairments: workshop plans, audio files and sets of exercises.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the lack of access to dance-related activities (especially forms of therapy based on dance and choreographic practice) for blind people.
sections.targetGroup: Blind and partially sighted people.
sections.whoCanUse: Blind and partially sighted people, facilities and organisations that can run such classes, cultural institutions.
sections.doesItWork: The solution makes it possible to change the way people think about organising and running dance and movement classes and creating dance performances for blind and partially sighted people. The project showed how much this type of class is needed in closed groups, for example in boarding houses for blind young people; during the classes, participants talked a lot about being treated like children at school, having no voice and no chance to make decisions about themselves.

c115.title: Zrozum moją kulturę, zrozum mnie (Understand my culture, understand me)

sections.solution: A method of working based on an integration game with refugees and migrants living in Poland who experience social exclusion because of cultural and social differences. The game includes, among other things, questions about culture, traditions and religion. By answering the questions, players earn points and share their own experiences with the other participants in the session.
sections.problems: The innovation responds to the social exclusion of refugees and the social and cultural barrier between immigrants and local people.
sections.targetGroup: Foreigners who live and work in Poland, refugees, and groups that are socially excluded because of cultural differences.
sections.whoCanUse: Schools, universities, community cultural centres and NGOs that work to integrate immigrant communities.
sections.doesItWork: As part of the innovation, an integration game was created, and playing it contributes measurably to reducing culture-related conflicts. While playing together, participants learn about the traditions and customs of different cultures, which helps to reduce mistrust and build curiosity towards difference.
